design: Fixed-lambda ridge logistic preference classifier; five-fold connected video/draft-group out-of-fold evaluation on clean labels only.

configuration.classBalancing: Each training draft is paired with its side-reversed opposite label; augmented classes exactly balanced.
configuration.scaling: RMS fitted only on each training fold; mirrored zero means; no intercept.
configuration.thresholdMeaning: Zero signed preference signal; exact numerical ties abstain. No threshold was selected using benchmark performance.

pairedComparison.caveat: Agreement rates at different coverage are not directly equivalent; this paired comparison uses only cases on which both models decide. It does not establish a statistically reliable improvement.

cleanDiagnostic.declaration: Product acceptance thresholds selected for this prototype; these are not thresholds stated by Kazewa. Passing this retrospective gate would still require prospective validation.

primary.declaration: Product acceptance thresholds selected for this prototype; these are not thresholds stated by Kazewa. Passing this retrospective gate would still require prospective validation.

model.interpretation: Signed preference signal learned from Kazewa labels; neither a calibrated preference probability nor a match win probability.

limitations: Only 62 clean historical cases are available; many labels include draft order, meta or player reasoning unavailable from compositions. The primary context-screened cohort has only five cases.

Group cross-validation prevents direct same-video and exact-draft leakage into training. It does not remove source overlap: the fixed features, taxonomy and expert rules were distilled from overlapping videos.
Regularization, 24 structural features, decision threshold and fold seed were fixed before scoring this experiment. This is a retrospective supervised experiment, not an untouched prospective test.
The logistic function is used only to optimize a preference classifier. Exported scores and coefficients are not calibrated win probabilities.
Case-level Wilson intervals do not account for correlation within groups. Fold variation and group counts are reported separately.
The full-data model is fitted to all clean labels; its training agreement is optimistic. Only grouped out-of-fold results estimate generalization within this historical corpus.

The exploratory full-review cohort is never used for training. Transfer results exclude every connected video/fingerprint group touching a clean training example, but annotations can still contain hindsight.
Correlated structural features make individual coefficient signs unstable and unsuitable for causal interpretation.
